name: Labor Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public labor and employment data.

entries.title: ABS Labour Force, Australia
entries.description: The Australian Bureau of Statistics' monthly headline labour market release from the Labour Force Survey: employment, unemployment, underemployment, participation and hours worked, nationally and by state and territory, in original, seasonally adjusted and trend terms.
entries.attribution: Source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Labour Force, Australia, <reference period>
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200, page "Labour Force, Australia, September 2026", "Headline estimates of employment, unemployment, underemployment, participation and hours worked from the monthly Labour Force Survey", released 15/10/2026. It reports that seasonally adjusted "the unemployment rate increased 0.1ppt to 4.7%" and notes that the September 2026 release "marks the return to the full suite of Labour Force data products" after the Labour Force Modernisation. The page has "Data downloads" sections; the spreadsheet format is assumed and wasn't opened. The ABS Data API and the series start years weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the ABS copyright page (https://www.abs.gov.au/website-privacy-copyright-and-disclaimer) says "All material presented on this website is provided under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence, with the exception of: the Commonwealth Coat of Arms, the ABS logo" and some other items. This is a site-wide statement that covers the data downloads. The attribution string follows the ABS's general guidance ("Attributing ABS material"), which wasn't opened.

entries.title: BLS Current Employment Statistics (CES)
entries.description: The monthly establishment survey behind the US nonfarm payroll jobs number: detailed industry estimates of employment, hours and earnings of workers on nonfarm payrolls, nationally and (through CES State and Metro Area) for all states and about 450 metropolitan areas.
entries.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), Department of Labor

access.auth_note: free registration key for higher BLS Public Data API limits (limits not checked)

coverage.spatial: United States (national; states and metropolitan areas through CES State and Metro Area)

entries.attribution: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Current Employment Statistics
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31 in headless Chromium: HTTP 200, page "Current Employment Statistics - CES (National)". It says "The Current Employment Statistics (CES) program produces detailed industry estimates of nonfarm employment, hours, and earnings of workers on payrolls." The latest releases listed are "Both payroll employment (+29,000) and unemployment rate (4.2%) change little in September" (10/02/2026) and "Preliminary benchmark revision for March payroll employment is -79,000 (-0.1%)" (08/28/2026). The page says The Employment Situation for October 2026 is due November 6, 2026. The formats and start years were not checked. bls.gov returned HTTP 403 "Access Denied" (Akamai) to curl with a browser user agent and to default headless Chromium. It answered only in Chromium's new headless mode (playwright chromium.launch with channel "chromium"), so the vertical needs reachability.headless: true and may need that launch mode. The BLS Public Data API (api.bls.gov) answered HTTP 200 but returned "REQUEST_NOT_PROCESSED ... daily threshold ... has been reached" for an unkeyed request through this shared proxy. Heavy use needs a free registration key, and the documented limits were not checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: BLS Copyright Information (https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm, read in headless Chromium) says "The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is a Federal government agency and everything that we publish, both in hard copy and electronically, is in the public domain, except for previously copyrighted photographs and illustrations. You are free to use our public domain material without specific permission, although we do ask that you cite the Bureau of Labor Statistics as the source." The BLS emblem is a registered trademark.

entries.title: BLS Consumer Price Index (CPI)
entries.description: The official US measure of consumer price inflation: the average change over time in the prices urban consumers pay for a market basket of goods and services, for the US and various metropolitan areas and regions, with average price data for selected food, fuel and utility items. Belongs here as the deflator for real wages; economy-almanac cross-references it.

entries.title: IBGE — Continuous National Household Sample Survey (PNAD Contínua), Brazil
entries.description: Brazil's continuous household survey and the source of the official unemployment rate (taxa de desocupação): quarterly and monthly (rolling-quarter) labour force, employment, informality and income indicators, plus annual supplements, published by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics.
entries.publisher: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

coverage.spatial: Brazil (national, regions, states, capitals and metropolitan areas)

entries.license: unverified — IBGE's terms pages on www.ibge.gov.br sit behind a Cloudflare challenge that could not be passed; no licence statement found on the reachable hosts
entries.attribution: Fonte: IBGE, Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for IBGE's file server listing "Index of /Trabalho_e_Rendimento/Pesquisa_Nacional_por_Amostra_de_Domicilios_continua", with folders Anual/, Mensal/, Trimestral/, Notas_metodologicas/, Nota_Tecnica/, Estudos_especiais/, Renda_domiciliar_per_capita/ and Principais_destaques_PNAD_continua/ (the last modified 2026-01-30). The SIDRA API answered HTTP 200 for table 4099, returning "Taxa de desocupação, na semana de referência, das pessoas de 14 anos ou mais de idade" = 5.4% for "2º trimestre 2026". The survey's IBGE page (https://www.ibge.gov.br/estatisticas/sociais/trabalho/9171-pesquisa-nacional-por-amostra-de-domicilios-continua-mensal.html), sidra.ibge.gov.br and agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br all returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." challenge to curl, headless Chromium and WebFetch, so the file server is cataloged instead; a curator may prefer the survey page once it can be verified. servicodados.ibge.gov.br reset the connection. The formats are inferred from the folder layout and the API response and weren't opened.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: not verified. No licence or terms text was reachable on IBGE's own hosts, so the licence is left unverified rather than guessed. The attribution string follows Brazilian convention and is not a quoted IBGE requirement.

entries.title: US Department of Labor Open Data Portal (enforcement and program data)
entries.description: The Department of Labor's open data portal, successor to enforcedata.dol.gov: Wage and Hour Division enforcement cases, OSHA inspections, violations and accident investigations, MSHA mine inspections and violations, EBSA case data, and unemployment insurance weekly claims, among other agency datasets.

access.auth_note: free account and API key required for the data API; the dataset-catalog endpoint needs no key; whether web downloads need sign-in was not checked

entries.attribution: U.S. Department of Labor, <agency> <dataset name>, DOL Open Data Portal
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200, page "Open Data Portal | United States Department of Labor" (marked "beta"), "Explore and download labor and workplace data". The old enforcement site https://enforcedata.dol.gov/views/data_summary.php now returns HTTP 301 to https://data.dol.gov:443/, so this entry catalogs the portal. Its keyless Datasets API (https://apiprod.dol.gov/v4/datasets) listed 45 datasets, including "WHD | Enforcement" (quarterly), OSHA Inspection, Violation, Violation Event and Accident tables (daily), eleven MSHA tables (weekly), EBSA OCATS (quarterly), and ETA unemployment insurance national and state weekly claims. The API user guide says "To use our APIs, you need to register for an account and complete our questionnaire to get an API key" and gives CSV and JSON endpoints. The formats come from those endpoint patterns; the individual downloads weren't opened.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: DOL's Public Domain Copyright page (https://www.dol.gov/general/aboutdol/copyright) says "Materials created by the federal government are generally part of the public domain and may be used, reproduced and distributed without permission ... You may properly credit public domain materials obtained from a DOL website to the U.S. Department of Labor and/or https://www.dol.gov." This is a department-wide statement, not a dataset-specific licence; it warns that some content may be third-party copyrighted.

entries.title: Eurostat Labour Market Database
entries.description: Eurostat's labour market statistics for the EU: the EU Labour Force Survey (employment, unemployment, working time, labour market slack), labour costs, earnings and the structure of earnings, job vacancies, and labour market policy data, harmonised across member states.

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries); NUTS regions for some series

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium), page "LABOUR MARKET Database" with "Selected datasets" and "Detailed datasets" trees and tabs for Overview, Publications, Information on data, Methodology and Legislation. The tree is collapsed in the page text, so the subject list in the description (LFS, labour costs, earnings, vacancies, LMP) follows Eurostat's usual theme structure and wasn't read item by item. A separate LFS database page (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/lfs/database) also answered HTTP 200; it is a subset of this theme, so it isn't cataloged separately. The quarterly cadence describes the headline LFS series; other datasets are annual or multi-annual. The formats and API weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) says "The copyright for the editorial content of this website, which is owned by the EU, is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence" and "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged." Third-party material is excluded. This matches the licence string used by the other Eurostat entries across the Almanac.

entries.title: ILOSTAT — ILO Labour Statistics Database
entries.description: The International Labour Organization's global labour statistics database: employment, unemployment, labour force, wages, working time, labour income, informality, occupational safety and labour-related SDG indicators, compiled from national sources and ILO modelled estimates for more than 200 countries and territories.

coverage.spatial: global (200+ countries and territories, plus regional and income-group aggregates)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (ILO Rights and permissions, data published as of 3 May 2023)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for the ILOSTAT API documentation (titled "ILOSTAT API", "Simple, comprehensive and direct access to ILOSTAT data", with examples for browser, R, Python, Stata and SAS). The main ILOSTAT portal (https://ilostat.ilo.org/data/) answered HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare "Just a moment..." challenge to curl, headless Chromium and WebFetch alike, so this entry catalogs the ILO-run API host; a curator may prefer to switch canonical_url back to the portal once it can be verified. On the same host, the ILOSTAT Bulk Download page (https://rplumber.ilo.org/files/website/bulk/indicator.html) showed "Last update: 2026-10-30" and lists .csv, .csv.gz, .dta, .feather, .rds, .parquet, .tsv and .json files, and a sample API call (unemployment rate, Canada, CSV) returned HTTP 200. ILO's own www.ilo.org/data-and-statistics page (HTTP 200) calls ILOSTAT "The world's leading source of labour statistics" with "300 million+ data points freely accessible".
Licence checked 2026-10-31: ILO Rights and permissions (https://www.ilo.org/rights-and-permissions, redirected from the API's "Copyright & permissions" link) says "As of 3 May 2023, databases and datasets together with the accompanying referential metadata are covered by the Creative Commons CC BY 4.0 licence. This licence does not apply to microdata submitted by or obtained from constituents and partner institutions that is restricted solely to the ILO's use." Data published before that date "do not automatically benefit from a Creative Commons licence". The ILOSTAT-specific terms page and citation format on ilostat.ilo.org could not be read (Cloudflare). Indicator coverage, start years and the cadence were not checked.
